title: Numbers and Overflow
goal: Learn integer types and safe arithmetic methods.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 1 Morning: Values and Variables

sections.text: Rust provides signed integer types like `i32` and unsigned types like `u8`. Integer literals without type annotations default to `i32`.

sections.caption: count is an 8-bit unsigned integer. default_num is i32.

sections.text: Rust never converts integer types implicitly. Mixing different integer types in expressions causes error `E0308`.

sections.code:
let score: u8 = 250;
let total = score.saturating_add(10);
sections.caption: saturating_add stays at 255 instead of overflowing.

sections.text: Standard arithmetic operators like `+` panic on overflow in debug builds. Explicit methods like `saturating_add` define safe behavior at boundary conditions.

explanation: Learn integer types and safe arithmetic methods.
